discoveries:
- D1 (interface) YAML 1.1 (PyYAML, which gov's front-matter reader uses) reads an unquoted key `on` as the boolean true. `waits_on: [{on: <id>, reason: ...}]` written plainly has no `on` key once read, so a schema requiring `on` refuses every such ticket. S19 asks T-1's skeleton, read as YAML, to give the keys `on` and `reason`: the template must quote `"on":`, or the interface renames the key.
- D2 (interface) .tickets/DAEO-2bdu.md already holds `waits_on:` as a list of strings ("DAEO-qskx — W2-142: ..."). A schema allowing only {on, reason} items turns it invalid, which the S10 guard catches (seen in the self-check). The S10 cases accept objects and refuse a bare string (not a list) and leave string items open, so anyOf(string, {on, reason}) satisfies both.
- D3 The register has 108 entries with status DONE (records of fact). F7 follows the brief ("not ACCEPTED"), so a DONE id in brackets fails it as a rule.
- D4 R3's T-0 front matter `role: {ROLE}` parses in YAML as a mapping, and R3's T-7 uses `{FACT:accepted_reds}`, a form outside the interface (read here as KEY FACT with a description, so keys.yaml must list FACT).
- D5 The interface does not say how a check form holding placeholders is filled. The runner fills tree keys with the temporary repository, BASE with HEAD, ID/W2/ROLE/PROFILE with this ticket's values and any other key from paths[key.lower()]; a key left fails by name (README). "A few seconds" is 5 s.
- D6 D5 row 6 (no gov retrieve in the sandbox) sits beside T-0's "Ask memory first: {CMD:retrieve}" line that S20 requires; the template has to state both. LINK-INTEGRITY §5 gives the CTO `gov links --since HEAD~1` while facts' links is `--since {BASE}`; S14 for T-8 asks only for HEAD~1 to appear.
- D7 F1 reads `gov <subcommand>` in a template's code: T-7/T-8 naming `gov context` (row 3) or a prohibition such as "never run `gov close`" in code needs a facts command holding it.
- D8 EMG-d4b-launched says the sandbox keeps tests/acceptance/ read-only; here writing tests/acceptance/W2-128/ worked.
- Exclusion line: every Grep, Glob and recursive search stayed inside this worktree (the one root-level Grep carried `!tests/acceptance/W2-128/**`); I listed the CTO tools folder in the main tree by `ls` (no search) to confirm the three scripts exist. No line of the implementation was seen; /home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-128 and w2/W2-128 were never opened.
risks: The string cases read units (paragraphs or list items; a line ending with a bracketed decision id ends one, a `Label:` line starts one); a writer who packs several rules into one unwrapped paragraph without decision ids at line ends lets a needle match across neighbouring rules. The check runner runs the real tools' check forms; a tool that needs more than 5 s on a loaded machine fails S6.
lessons: Build a stand-in from the spec and mutate it before committing: it found the YAML `on:` key and the DAEO-2bdu clash, and a units rule that let a Start line borrow the next line's words.
proposed_decisions:
- P1 (D1) Options: (a) T-1 quotes `"on":` and the schema keeps `on` (cost: a pitfall every ticket writer meets; the ready check could warn); (b) rename the key to `id:` or `ref:` (cost: an interface change before round 2, a test revision). Recommendation (b), confidence medium.
- P2 (D2) Options: (a) waits_on items anyOf(string, {on, reason}) (cost: two forms); (b) re-write DAEO-2bdu's waits_on to the object form in the same change (cost: a ticket edit, the CTO's lane, TICKET_CHANGE_UNMARKED unless marked). Recommendation (a), confidence medium.
unresolved: S6's TPL-2 S3, S10's TPL-5 S3, S19's refusals, S17's review/approval/promotion, and S7, S9, S11-S13, F2-F6 are round 2 or later CIT-P steps (README).
recommended_next_action: The CTO writes TESTS-READY for round 1, takes P1 and P2 before the product-spec writer fixes T-1's waits_on form, and merges these tests into the product-spec worker's branch outside the sandbox.
